paragraphs: Gaggle sells student safety services to schools, with a stated mission of ensuring the safety and well-being of students and schools through people and technology. Its core product uses machine learning and trained safety experts to analyze student-created content in school-issued accounts and devices.

A web filter blocks inappropriate content and automatically categorizes new sites as it scans them. A therapy service connects students with licensed mental health professionals for weekly teletherapy sessions. A round-the-clock service called ReachOut gives students direct access to confidential care whenever they need support. An archiving product stores files and communications in one searchable, cloud-based system so districts can meet compliance obligations.

The company says it has been supporting student safety and well-being for more than 20 years. Its founder started the company as a secure student email provider in 1998. It describes itself as the pioneer in helping K-12 districts manage student safety on school-provided technology. The home page puts its reach at over 1,500 K-12 districts, and one case study describes a district choosing the therapy service to meet growing student mental health needs.

quote.text: Gaggle’s mission is to ensure the safety and well-being of students and schools by leveraging people and technology.
